name: What is the difference between a slab-on-grade and a raised foundation?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a slab-on-grade and a raised foundation?

acceptedAnswer.text: A slab-on-grade foundation is a single layer of concrete poured directly on a prepared ground surface, often with a thickened edge. It's common in warmer climates like Las Vegas due to its cost-effectiveness and quick installation. A raised foundation (or pier-and-beam/crawl space) involves constructing a perimeter stem wall or piers that elevate the structure, creating a crawl space beneath. This allows for easier access to plumbing and electrical systems, and can be beneficial in areas prone to expansive soils.
acceptedAnswer.description: Slab-on-grade is concrete directly on the ground; a raised foundation elevates the structure, creating a crawl space for access and soil considerations.
